statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band well below the block threshold, while Stress remains elevated on an active energy and geopolitical backdrop.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping resolves to EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD alike. A narrow danger window is flagged for the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC, where two sessions of accumulated Middle East and energy news are discounted in a single auction. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Oil-led geopolitical stress, but Nasdaq futures stay orderly and two-sided
body: U.S. cash equity markets were shut on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, so the Nasdaq-100 last closed at 29,544.15 on 4 September. Over the intervening period the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, and Saudi Aramco's 400,000 barrel-per-day Jizan refinery was reported hit for the third time in two months. Brent traded above $97 and WTI above $92, six-to-seven week highs after a roughly 10% weekly energy advance. The transmission into index risk is nevertheless narrow: NQ futures are near 29,586, up about 0.07%, sitting mid-range inside a 29,525-29,682 band with no observed one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed retracement. VIX at 15.30 is a low absolute volatility regime, gold is slightly lower rather than bid, Treasury futures are close to unchanged and the 10-year constant maturity was last published at 4.77%. Cross-asset alignment is therefore absent: the Nasdaq is outperforming the Dow because the shock is energy-led, and semiconductor strength is offsetting megacap and software softness. That combination supports elevated Stress with Tail held in the low band. The principal forward checkpoint is the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening, which must absorb the accumulated escalation in one auction, followed by PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours were published continuously with Tail between 5 and 10 and the mapped state green throughout. Stress stepped up from the mid-50s during the Asian and European hours of 7 September into the low 60s from roughly 14:00 UTC onward, as the weekend U.S.-Iran escalation and the Aramco Jizan report moved crude to multi-week highs. Confidence eased from the mid-80s to the mid-to-high 70s across the same stretch, reflecting the Labor Day cash closure and the resulting absence of U.S. cash breadth and volume evidence. The dominant mode alternated between normal and mixed and at no point registered persistent directional efficiency.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour path is shaped by one dominant scheduled feature: the U.S. cash reopening at 13:30 UTC after the Labor Day closure, which must price two sessions of accumulated Middle East and energy news in a single auction. Conditional Tail is held in the low band through the Asian and European hours, rises to a session peak of 18 across 13:00-15:00 UTC, then decays through the U.S. afternoon as price discovery is expected to become orderly. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape, moving into the high band from 12:00 UTC and easing back to the elevated band after the cash close. Every hour maps to EA_ON because no persistent no-retracement structure is observed and cross-asset confirmation is absent. The stated conditional invalidation is repeated extension after failed retracements with NQ holding near session extremes; a fresh Hormuz supply discontinuity is the identified unscheduled revision source. PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September sit beyond this horizon.
